newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police raid Islamic centres in crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police raid Islamic centres in crackdown.

text.p: Turkish police raided illegal Islamic education centres as Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan stalled on an anti-Islamist crackdown that has rocked his government, security officials said on Monday.

It was the first confirmed report of concrete action since the secularist army demanded a crackdown against an Islamic revival two months ago. Halting illegal Islamic education is one of the generals' main demands.
Police in the western province of Bursa swooped on seven buildings housing unofficial Koranic education courses on Sunday, a spokesman for the governor's office said.
"The courses were closed," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone. "They were found to be operating outside the writ of the religious affairs directorate," he said.
The Islamist prime minister signed a National Security Council communique on Saturday agreeing to go ahead with the curbs on the role of Islam in public life.
But senior MP in Erbakan's Welfare Party have said they will try to block any bid by parliament to restrict religious school education.
The Milliyet daily on Monday quoted an unnamed senior military officer as criticising Erbakan for his delaying tactics.
